EXECUTIVE ORDER 10125
Creating  an  E m ergency  B oard T o I nves ­
tigate  a D ispute  B e t w e e n the  C hicago  
& I l lin o is M idland  R a il w a y C o m p a n y 
and  C ertain  of  I ts  E m plo y e e s
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Chicago &  Illinois Midland Railway 
Company, a carrier, and certain of its 
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a large section of the country 
of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by 
me, to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pecu­
niarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Chicago & Hlinois Midland 
Railway Company or its employees in 
the conditions out of which the said dis­
pute arose.
H arry  S. T r um an
Chapter IV— Production and Market­
ing Administration and Commodity

Agriculture

[Amdt. 4]

TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF FRESH APPLE  
EXPORT PROGRAM; EXTENDING FINAL DATES
Eligibility for payment.  The final date 
filing Form FV-427, “Declaration of Sale 
and Intent To Export Fresh Apples Un­
der Program QMX 96a” (as provided in 
§ 517.104 (a) ), shall be 12:00 o’clock mid­
night May 31, 1950.
The final date of export (as provided 
in § 517.104 (c) ) is hereby extended to 
12:00 o’clock midnight May 31, 1950.
Claims supported by proof of exporta­
tion. The final date for filing claims 
for payment (Form FDA-564, “Public 
Voucher-Diversion Programs,” and sup­
porting documents, as provided in 
§  517.105 (a) ) is hereby extended to 
12:00 o’clock midnight June 30, 1950.
Effective date.  This amendment shall 
become effective at 12:01 a. m., e. s. t., 
April 25, 1950.
(Sec. 32, 49 Stat. 774r as amended, sec. 112,  
62 Stat. 146; 7 U. S. C. and Sup., 612c)
Dated this 24th day of April 1950.
[ seal ] S. R. S m it h,
Authorized Representative of  
the Secretary of Agriculture.
{F. R. Doc. 50-3600; Filed. Apr. 27, 1950;  
8:46 a. m.]

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10125 at 15 FR 2391 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 26, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1950 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 672 to 3814 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10125 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10125_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10125_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_d68f78cdf2.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated May 19, 1950. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking May 19, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on May 19, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to June 18, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; the order created a board for one dispute and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown, and section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues on its own force. The bounded search covered the held text of Executive Order 12553, the order's own text and the OFR catalog disposition notes.
